validated_results.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
validated_results.reason: Large multiethnic prospective cohort reporting hazard ratios per 1 SD increase in DASH diet score for incident prostate cancer, including a specific DASH estimate among African Americans.

extraction.comparison_type: per 1 SD increase in DASH score, advanced prostate cancer among African Americans
extraction.ethnicity: White, African American, Japanese American, Latino, or Native Hawaiian
extraction.population: 79,930 men in the Multiethnic Cohort study

sample_size.excerpt: In the Multiethnic Cohort study, we examined associations between 11 diet scores and prostate cancer risk among 79,930 men (White, African American, Japanese American, Latino, or Native Hawaiian).

cases.excerpt: Over a mean follow-up of 18.8 years, 9,759 prostate cancer cases were identified.

effect_size.excerpt: However, among African Americans, higher Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension scores were suggestively associated with a 14% lower risk of advanced prostate cancer (95% CI, 0.77-0.98; P = 0.02). Among Japanese Americans, higher Empirical Dietary Index for Insulin Resistance scores were linked to an increased risk of low-grade (HR = 1.09; 95% CI, 1.02-1.17; P = 0.01) and nonaggressive prostate cancer (HR = 1.10; 95% CI, 1.02-1.19; P = 0.02).

confidence_interval.excerpt: However, among African Americans, higher Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension scores were suggestively associated with a 14% lower risk of advanced prostate cancer (95% CI, 0.77-0.98; P = 0.02).
